Single-cut baseline and up-enumerated stereo records are compared row for row against a committed mmpdb 3.1.4 oracle, and match for every fixture structure. The fixture now includes the two shapes that once diverged at baseline: 1,4-disubstituted rings whose cis/trans stereo is dependent rather than independently chiral, and parent SMILES carrying a stereo tag that describes nothing. mmpdb keys its dedupe on attachment_order.variable_smiles.constant_smiles without the enumeration label, which restores the rows its frag1_indices reference defect would otherwise suppress, so that defect is unobservable at one cut. The match is a statement about the fixture, not about every input: single-cut output carries whatever the cleanup pass decided about the parent, so the residual classes recorded on the clear_fragmentation_invalidated_stereo row flow straight through it -- ring sulfoxides and selenoxides, bridged bicyclics such as tropanes, quinuclidines and adamantanes including bridgehead nitrogen, three-coordinate phosphorus, acyclic pseudo-asymmetric centres such as ribitol, and metal complexes. None of those shapes is in the fixture, so they are unobserved here rather than matched. The residual is scheduled for a follow-on fix.

Potential-stereocentre detection is exercised through the fixture: centres that survive a cut, a specified tag that is not a real centre and collapses to one achiral form, prochiral carbons that a cut desymmetrises into new centres, and the three-coordinate nitrogen shapes upstream refuses to call chiral. OEMMPA applies the same shape rule as RDKit isAtomPotentialChiralCenter, which mmpdb transcribes: four heavy neighbours always qualify, three qualify with exactly one hydrogen, and three with no hydrogen qualify only for sulfur or selenium at a sulfoxide-like valence.

Partly covered. The dependent ring-stereo classes RDKit pairs are handled and are in the fixture: 1,4-disubstituted rings such as C[C@H]1CC[C@@H](O)CC1, 1,3-disubstituted cyclobutanes, macrocyclic pairs such as 1,5-disubstituted cyclooctane, and pairs spanning a spiro junction, alongside the lone tags and the invalid geminal E/Z marker that have to be cleared. OEMMPA reproduces the RDKit rule as a pairing rule rather than by symmetry refinement: a tagged, non-chiral ring atom whose two ring neighbours are symmetry equivalent keeps its tag only when another such atom shares its ring system, so half a pair is still cleared. Measured against RDKit's parse-time cleanup over 8000 stereo-bearing SureChEMBL structures, dropped-stereo cases fall from 360 to 222 with no regressions, so a residual divergence class remains. Residual: ring sulfoxides and selenoxides, because RDKit's ring-stereo candidate rule admits an atom with one non-ring neighbour and two ring neighbours, so C[C@H]1CC[S@](=O)CC1 keeps both tags in RDKit and loses both here; bridged bicyclics such as tropanes, quinuclidines and adamantanes, including bridgehead nitrogen, because a partner with three ring bonds is not a candidate under the exactly-two-ring-bonds rule; three-coordinate phosphorus; acyclic pseudo-asymmetric centres such as ribitol; and metal complexes. The residual is scheduled for a follow-on fix.

Parents whose stereo tag describes nothing (C[C@H](C)CO, a tag on a carbon carrying two identical methyls) are in the fixture and match record for record and label for label. RDKit clears such a tag while parsing, so everything downstream in mmpdb works on the normalised parent; OEMMPA reproduces that by normalising a copy of the parent before cut selection, which restores both the achiral baseline records and the up-enumerated records the phantom tag previously suppressed.

Created-stereocentre up-enumeration matches mmpdb for every enumerating fixture structure. N,N-dialkylamine and N,N-dialkylsulfonamide motifs are in the fixture rather than excluded from it: a cut that leaves a three-coordinate nitrogen with no hydrogen creates no stereocentre, because the shape rule OEMMPA now shares with mmpdb is_potential_chiral_center admits three neighbours and no hydrogen only for sulfur and selenium.

Ring-constrained and exocyclic E/Z geometry is verified against the oracle. Acyclic stereogenic double bonds are out of fixture scope: mmpdb asymmetric begin/end bond-direction transfer inverts exactly one of the two cuts flanking such a bond, and RDKit FragmentOnBonds agrees with OEMMPA rather than mmpdb there, so an acyclic case would pin an upstream error.

Explicit design difference. The mmpdb fragment command never produces hydrogen fragmentations; only transform and predict call this surface, and only they emit its `[*][H]` _hydrogen_cut_smiles constant. The committed oracle therefore contains none, and a structural test (a projected fragment with no heavy atom) pins the absence so it cannot become an unnoticed coverage gap.
